messages:
maria: Heads-up — nightly perf run shows a regression after the runtime change landed last night. median token latency up ~2.3x on long-context chat jobs. nsys shows weird gaps in kernel scheduling (lots of idle time between matmul launches).

raj: oof. any quick diffs from before/after traces? perfetto heatmap or nsys timeline would help.

maria: attaching two traces (before vs after) in the artifacts bucket: https://artifacts.internal/redwood/traces/1844999000_before.nsight and https://artifacts.internal/redwood/traces/1845000000_after.nsight

ken: saw the diff in batcher lately — we changed the batching heuristic to wait an extra 4ms before flushing when sequence length variance is high. Could that increase stray kernel gaps?

lina: that sounds plausible. extra wait could cause suboptimal packing, leaving kernels with smaller launches and then idle. can you share the perfetto heatmap?

maria: pasted the heatmap snapshot inline: ```perfetto: heatmap (timeline) - before: dense continuous kernels; after: vertical stripes of idle between launches```

sam: quick check: is KV cache eviction behavior involved? if the cache misses increase, we might be reloading KV tensors and forcing kernel memory ops.

maria: KV hit-rate unchanged per metrics. timeline shows kernel launch spacing rather than big memcpy ops.

raj: cool. let's bisect the change set. what range includes the batching heuristic tweak?

ken: PR #5123 touched batcher/windowing and also touched scheduler fallback ordering. suspect commits: 4f2a9b -> 7d3e1c -> 9a8b2f.

maria: starting bisect:
```
git bisect start 9a8b2f 4f2a9b
# run nightly perf job script/prof/run_profile.sh --model chat-xl --ctx 8k
# collect nsys -o /tmp/trace_after.nsys
```

ci-bot: bisect job queued on runner r-gpu-12 (ETA ~15m).

(15m later)

maria: first bisect pass: good at 7d3e1c, bad at 9a8b2f => narrows to 9a8b2f..7d3e1c. testing 8b7c4d next.

ken: 8b7c4d is the batching window change. fwiw it was intended to reduce tail latency by letting batches fill, but maybe it backfired with our kernel placement heuristics.

maria: ran nsys on 8b7c4d. timeline: more frequent small kernels, kernel occupancy lower, long gaps between kernels of the same stream. link: https://artifacts.internal/redwood/traces/1845000100_8b7c4d.nsys

lina: can you run the kernel selector trace with debug flags? there are logs about chosen kernel variant per launch. command: ```RUNTIME_DEBUG=kernel_select:1 ./serve --trace-kernels > kernel_trace.log```

maria: ran that. snippet from kernel_trace.log: ```[kernel_select] seq_len=2048 -> variant=matmul_f16_smalltiles (forced) waiting_for_batch_window(ms)=12 -> launch_delay=9ms```

sam: aha. smalltiles variant has higher per-launch overhead and worse concurrency when launches aren't coalesced. The window increase meant more launches fell into small batches that hit smalltiles instead of largetiles.

raj: so the regression is from the batching window bump causing the selector to pick smalltile kernels due to smaller effective batch size. that increases kernel overhead and gaps.

ken: agree. fix options: revert batching window change, or adjust kernel selector threshold (prefer largetiles unless batch count < X), or change batcher to prefer coalescing by quickly filling early when many requests queued.

maria: quick experiment: I patched kernel selector to bias toward largetiles by lowering threshold: ```if (effective_batch >= 4) prefer=largetiles``` and re-ran profile. baseline restored (latency back to before). trace: https://artifacts.internal/redwood/traces/1845000200_patch_select.nsys

lina: nice. that probably mitigates without reverting. we should still evaluate tail latency tradeoffs for small convo users.

sam: output from the compare script: ```./perf/compare_traces.py before.nsight after.nsight --metric median_token_latency``` gave: before=48ms token, after=112ms, patched=52ms. CPU/GPU utilization graphs also match.

maria: next steps: (1) revert batching-window tweak in canary until we land robust selector heuristics, (2) open a follow-up PR to make selector thresholds adaptive to batch distribution, (3) add an nsys perf test to CI that asserts no >1.5x regression for median token latency on long-context model.

ken: i'll draft PR to revert the window change and add commentary linking the kernel_selector fix.

raj: can we add an automated trace check that scans for kernel launch gaps ( >5ms idle ) per-stream and fails the perf job when regression appears? we can include perfetto heatmap diff thresholds.

maria: yes — filing perf ticket: PF-1423 and attaching traces. Also creating a short runbook entry for diagnosing similar regressions: steps to bisect, trace commands, key logs to grep (`kernel_select`, `batch_window_ms`, `effective_batch`).

sam: fyi I'll post a short note in #eng-runtime when revert PR is up. :thumbsup:

ci-bot: revert PR #5180 opened by ken -> https://git.internal/redwood/pull/5180

maria: thanks all. summary: regression root cause = batching-window bump -> smaller effective batches -> kernel selector picks high-overhead smalltile kernels -> creates scheduling gaps -> latency regression. mitigated by selector bias to prefer large tiles; reverting batching change for canary until we land more robust adaptive selector.

ken: will follow up with perf numbers in PR.

lina: great detective work. saved the rollout. :tada:
